subject: Prorated tranche alignment & billing for multi-year Dedicated commit
messages:
From: Katie Morgan <katie.morgan@argoscale.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, procurement@argoscale.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity — billing/proration question

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We're excited about the Dedicated offering but need to align on two things before procurement signs off:

1) Ramp proration — ArgoScale plans a 36-month committed term but wants the first 6 months to be a gradual onramp (start at 25% GPU/TPM, step to 60% at month 3, full by month 7). Can Redwood prorate prepay credits so we only pay fully for capacity once it's live, or do you require full prepayment for the committed term?

2) Term discount stacking — we were quoted a 15% term discount for a 3-year prepay; our counsel is asking whether customer-side accelerator credits (early-payment credits or milestone credits) can combine with that discount or if discounts are mutually exclusive.

If helpful, procurement has attached our internal ramp plan (we'll send the formal SOW after we lock the billing model). Can you share a simple example showing amortization / invoicing for the first year with the proposed ramp?

Appreciate a clear, itemized example we can pass to finance.

Best,
Katie
Procurement — ArgoScale

Attachment: argoscale_ramp_outline.xlsx (attachment referenced)

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katie Morgan <katie.morgan@argoscale.com>
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-03T10:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — billing/proration question

Hi Katie — thanks for the clear summary. I spoke to Finance and Pricing and put together two pragmatic options that keep your ramp flexibility while preserving Redwood's capacity planning. See the attached: argoscale_term_sheet_v3.pdf and ramp_schedule_proposal.xlsx. Short summary below.

Option A — Prorated Prepay + Milestone Invoice:
- You prepay a pro-rated portion for the committed GPU/TPM based on the first 12 months forecasted utilization (we can cap at 80% of committed in year 1 to reflect onramp).
- Monthly invoices reconcile actual usage vs amortized prepay; if you underutilize, remaining credits roll forward but are subject to a 6% annual decay to incentivize timely scale (can be negotiated).
- Term discount: 15% stack applies to the committed prepay amount. Milestone/acceleration credits are additive (we can provide up to 5% acceleration credit when you hit a launch milestone).

Option B — Full Prepay with Built-in Ramp Credits:
- Full 36-month prepay at 15% term discount, but we reserve a 10% buffer of credits held in escrow and released based on month-by-month ramp milestones.
- If ramp slows, buffer credits are returned on a quarterly reconciliation.

Key considerations: we can accommodate a 25% start → 60% → 100% ramp cadence; finance needs explicit monthly forecasts for year 1 to produce amortization schedule. I've modeled a sample amortization (sheet tab 'Year1_amort') showing monthly invoices and credit balances.

Next step ask: if Option A looks promising, can you send the month-level forecast for the first 9 months by EOD Thursday? If not, we'll iterate on Option B mechanics.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with Pricing and Finance if useful.

— Olga
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Attachment: argoscale_term_sheet_v3.pdf; ramp_schedule_proposal.xlsx

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-05T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — billing/proration question

Olga / Priyom — quick finance note for the thread:

- We can support Option A but need a conservative recognition rule for the first 12 months. Suggest Redwood recognizes revenue against the committed amount but defers the portion tied to an explicit ramp milestone (i.e., the 25%→60% step). That means we'd book revenue monthly on actual validated usage up to the amortized prepaid amount.
- The 6% annual decay on rolled credits feels high; propose 3% or replace decay with a clause that returns unused credits at year boundaries.
- Acceleration credits: treat as contra-revenue (applied on invoices) and cap total accelerator exposure at 7% of ARR for the deal to maintain portfolio-level guardrails.

I'll draft updated language for the term sheet if we agree these constraints.

-Rishi
VP, Finance Operations

On May 3, 2027, at 10:07 AM, Olga Petrov wrote:
> Hi Katie — thanks for the clear summary. I spoke to Finance and Pricing and put together two pragmatic options...

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwoodinference.com>
To: Katie Morgan <katie.morgan@argoscale.com>, olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-05-07T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — billing/proration question

Katie — thanks for the patience while we assessed internally. A few practical clarifications from a commercial standpoint:

- For procurement ease, we recommend Option A but packaged as "Prorated Prepay with Milestone Credits" on the PO. That lets your procurement sign a single PO referencing the total committed units and a schedule of milestone releases.
- Example amortization (excerpt):
  * Contract: 36 months, committed 100 TPM equivalent, 15% term discount on prepay.
  * Year 1 forecast: months 1-2 at 25 TPM, months 3-6 ramp to 60 TPM, months 7-12 at 100 TPM.
  * Invoice cadence: monthly. Month 1 invoice = (prepay amort month 1) - (milestone credit if month 3 launch achieved).
- We can provide a single line item on the invoice for "Committed prepay amortization" and a separate line "Milestone credit applied" so your AP team sees net amounts.

Operational ask: Can your legal team accept language allowing Redwood to reconcile usage quarterly and return unused credits on each anniversary? We prefer that to decay.

If procurement agrees, I can update the term sheet and send a redline to counsel. Happy to take a 30-minute call to walk through the sample amort schedule.

Thanks,
Priyom
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Katie Morgan <katie.morgan@argoscale.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@argoscale.com, legal@argoscale.com
Date: 2027-05-10T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity — billing/proration question

Thanks — that framing is helpful. Procurement and Legal prefer:

- Option A with reconciliation at each 12-month anniversary (no decay).
- Acceleration credits are fine if we can cap them at 5% and have them applied only after an "availability" milestone is signed off by both parties (to avoid subjective gating).
- We will provide the month-level forecast for the first 9 months by COB Friday (sending as CSV).

One request from Finance: can Redwood provide a worked example showing net cashflow across months 1–12 (invoice amounts and cash application) so we can reconcile on our side? If you can include the DocuSign-ready term sheet, we'll get procurement to sign quickly.

Appreciate the responsiveness — Katie
Procurement, ArgoScale

Katie — great, thanks for the confirmation. Attached is a worked cashflow example (tab 'cashflow_1-12' in ramp_schedule_proposal.xlsx) and a DocuSign-ready term sheet link in the related_links.

Summary of agreed commercial points for the term sheet (I will send a redline to counsel and the DocuSign envelope once we confirm):
- Contract: 36 months, committed 100 TPM equivalent (GPU-backed)
- Pricing: 15% term discount on prepay amount
- Billing model: Option A (Prorated Prepay + Milestone Credits); Redwood will amortize prepay monthly and invoice monthly; unused credits are reconciled and returned at each 12-month anniversary (no decay).
- Acceleration credits: capped at 5% of total prepay; released only after mutually agreed availability milestone sign-off; applied as invoice-level credit (contra-revenue).
- Reconciliation: quarterly usage validation; annual credit return if underutilized.
- Invoicing: single line for amortization + separate credit line for transparency.

Next actions:
1) Katie — send the 9-month month-level forecast (CSV).
2) Priyom — I'll send the redline to ArgoScale counsel once forecast is received.
3) Rishi / Finance — I'll include your contra-revenue cap language in the term sheet redline.

Looking forward — will follow up with DocuSign link shortly.

— Olga
Head of Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
